 Previewing the top IHSA football playoff quarterfinals
 A look at this weekend’s best games.
 By  
 Mike Clark

 Fenwick quarterback Myles Hill (15) scrambles for a gain before Brayden Parks (98) and Manny Uriarte (0) bring him down.

 Class 8A: No. 4 Mount Carmel at No. 1 Lincoln-Way East 
 1 p.m. Saturday: Based on the teams’ talent and résumés, this matchup feels more like a state semifinal or even a state final. But losses to East St. Louis and Brother Rice dropped Mount Carmel (9-2) to a No. 8 seed, and here we are. Brady Cloherty, who started the season as the Caravan’s No. 2 quarterback, already has set the program’s single-season record for touchdown passes, aided by the deepest receiving corps in the state. That group includes Michigan commit Quentin Burrell, Marshaun Thornton and Ty Kennedy. Mount Carmel’s defense has stars at all three levels with lineman Caleb Tucker, linebacker Roman Igwebuike (Notre Dame) and defensive back Tavares Harrington (Michigan). All Lincoln-Way East (11-0) has done is win, with signature victories against Brother Rice, Kankakee, Homewood-Flossmoor and more. The Griffins beat Oak Park and Hinsdale Central the last two weeks with backup quarterback Tyler Sychalski filling in for Evan LeFevour.
 Class 8A: No. 7 Bolingbrook at No. 8 Oswego 
 5 p.m. Saturday: This is a rematch of Bolingbrook’s 21-7 victory in Week 4. A season-opening shutout loss to Homewood-Flossmoor is just a distant memory for Bolingbrook (10-1), which is led by two of the top players in the state in running back TJ Lewis (Oklahoma State) and edge rusher Darieon Prescott (Notre Dame). Lewis had one of the plays of the year in a 22-14 victory last week against Lyons, a zigging-and-zagging, 73-yard run that took him from one sideline to the other. Oswego (10-1), the Class 8A runner-up last year, is succeeding behind its usual mix of swarming defense and effective running by Ammar Banire, quarterback Drew Kleinhans and fullback Luke Hernandez.
 Class 6A: No. 23 Wheaton North vs. No. 21 Fenwick 
 1 p.m. Saturday at Triton: Wheaton North (8-3) is coming off the biggest upset in the playoffs, a down-to-the-wire, 36-35 victory against Geneva that avenged a 42-14 loss in Week 7. Sophomore quarterback Grant Neibch, who was promoted to the varsity in Week 6 after older brother Burke went out with a hand injury, threw the game-winning touchdown pass to Johnny Clayton with 7.8 seconds left. Iowa recruit Jake Thies, arguably the best two-way player in the state as a running back and defensive back, has a program-record 44 career touchdowns and counting for defending Class 6A champ Fenwick (8-3).
 Class 5A: St. Francis at No. 25 Cary-Grove 
 1 p.m. Saturday: Defending Class 5A champion St. Francis (7-5) is one of two five-loss teams still alive (Nazareth is the other). Since losing to Montini in Week 9, the Spartans have averaged more than 50 points in three lopsided playoff victories. Running back Tivias Caldwell Jr., quarterback Jadon Wilson, wide receiver Greg Bess-Henning and two-way star James McGrath (Western Illinois) are among St. Francis’ playmakers. Despite coming into the season with one of coach Brad Seaburg’s least experienced teams, Cary-Grove (9-2) is in the quarterfinals for the seventh time since 2018. Quarterback Jackson Berndt has the Trojans’ trademark triple-option offense humming along.
 Class 3A: No. 6 IC Catholic at Byron 
 2:30 p.m. Saturday: This might wind up being the de facto Class 3A title game. IC Catholic (10-1) has lost only to Class 8A power Loyola in a game the Knights led at halftime. Running back Jakobe Baldwin has rushed for more than 1,500 yards with 17 touchdowns, and Grant Bowen, a top-40 player nationally in the junior class, has more than 800 receiving yards with 11 TDs. Byron (11-0) won the game between the teams last year 28-6 en route to its third state title since 2021. The Tigers have an average winning margin of 45 points this season.
